newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro completes Anchor Glass sale.
newsitem.headline: Vitro completes Anchor Glass sale.

text.p: Mexican glassmaker Vitro SA said it completed on Wednesday the sale of its U.S. subsidiary Anchor Glass Container Corp to Consumer Packaging Inc and Owens-Brookway Glass Container.

It said the proceeds of the sale, including $328.8 million in cash, $47 million in face value of 10 percent cumulative convertible preferred stock and 490,898 common stock of the succesor to Anchor, will be used to repay Anchor's creditors.

Vitro said that to facilitate the sale, it provided the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp (PBGC) a guarantee of Anchor's underfunding liability limited to $70 million, payable after five years in semi-annual installments over 10 years.

But it said no payments would be made unless the successor to Anchor fails to comply with its pension obligations and the PBGC terminates any of Anchor's three pension plans. "Even then the guarantee be payable only to the extent the PBGC could not recover from the successor to Anchor the underfunding liabilities," it added.
The amount and the term of the guarantee will be proportionally reduced if the pension plans are terminated after five years from closing.
Anchor Glass filed for Chapter 11 protection in Sept. 1996. The U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Delaware has approved of the sale.
